newsitem.title: USA: Asahi probe involves no monetary losses.
newsitem.headline: Asahi probe involves no monetary losses.

text.p: A probe of activities at the New York office of Asahi Bank Ltd does not involve any monetary losses to either the bank or its customers, a bank spokesman said Friday.
The spokesman said he could not make any further comment about the investigation.

Sources familiar with the investigation said the investigation was focusing on allegations that at least two executives of the New York branch read confidential documents regarding an examination of the bank.
During examinations, which can take weeks to complete, officials leave their working papers at the bank overnight.
Examiners discovered last summer that material relating to an earlier examination had been read, the sources said.
Since that time, Kazuhiro Shibatsuchi, the general manager of the branch, was replaced in that post by Katsumi Sakai. Shibatsuchi has remained in New York waiting for reassignments.
It could not be determined if there was a connection between the investigation and the replacement of Shibatsuchi as head of the New York branch.
A spokesman for the U.S. Attorney's office declined comment on a published report that examiners had referred the Asahi investigation to prosecutors for possible criminal charges.
The New York State Banking Department and the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, both of which have responsibility for oversight of the bank's New York office, declined comment.
